title: Why Is TypeScript Used? knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the role of TypeScript in a development workflow?
options: It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
It replaces the JavaScript runtime in every browser.
It validates all network data automatically.
It removes the need for runtime tests.
questions.answer_key: It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
questions.explanation: Type checking is a development-time layer and does not replace runtime verification.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Why Is TypeScript Used?”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with detecting errors before execution and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with detecting errors before execution and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Detecting errors before execution”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Why Is TypeScript Used?”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check improving code navigation and editor assistance, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume supporting maintainable applications and large codebases is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check improving code navigation and editor assistance, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Improving code navigation and editor assistance”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
